why: Check 1's expect line asks only that --tsv print the same JSON array the CSV run prints for the same table. The non-empty `[ "$a" = "$b" ]` → SAME test covers that. But the PASS condition also requires "the csv line is a JSON array of the two rows: [{"name":"ann","age":"30"},{"name":"bob","age":"41"}]". That fixes exact values, key order and string types for the CSV path, which the expect line doesn't require. A PR whose TSV and CSV outputs match but differ from that literal would wrongly FAIL. That requirement belongs under Advisory. Check 2 (grep for --tsv plus describing the flag) fits "documents --tsv". The Advisory section correctly holds npm test, whether a test was added, and the no-flag CSV regression check. Because Check 1's PASS condition is too strict, the criterion is not met.
